title: Protected treasury balance lock transaction boundary: initial purchase versus payroll payment
scope: Bounded semantic comparison of initial ReceivePurchase and PayPayroll balance checks, with PayPurchase and AddExpense as transaction-boundary controls and the shared TreasuryBalanceQuery contract. Does not audit every balance-query caller.

behavior.initial_purchase: ReceivePurchaseHandler validates the payment amount and account, then for an account id calls LoadAccountMovementsForUpdateAsync and AssertProtectedSourceBalance at lines 77-78. It reads cost basis and checks the business day, and only starts its database transaction at line 97. Later the transaction writes purchase/payment, optional treasury movement, supplier ledger, stock receipt movements, audit and journal completion (lines 100-208). Thus the helper lock is not held across the later posting transaction in this call sequence.
behavior.payroll_control: PayPayrollHandler checks Approved and computes payroll total first, then opens its transaction before calling the same balance-lock helper at lines 110-119. The guarded movement, employee settlements, Paid run state, journal and audit are saved and committed within that transaction (121-163).
behavior.purchase_payment_control: PayPurchaseHandler checks open business day and begins its transaction before the same helper call (71-81); payment movement and supplier ledger update occur in that transaction.
behavior.expense_control: AddExpenseHandler begins a transaction before loading the account movements and asserting the protected source balance (69-78); the expense and movement are written in the same transaction.
behavior.shared_lock_contract: TreasuryBalanceQuery documents that LoadAccountMovementsForUpdateAsync uses SQL Server UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK range locks and requires the caller already to be inside a transaction; the lock is released when the transaction ends. It exists to serialize competing inserts affecting an account balance.

counterevidence_and_limits: A transaction and idempotency/journal key protect atomicity and same-request replay for each purchase; the comparison does not establish duplicate purchase or a realized overdraft.
PayPayroll and PayPurchase demonstrate the transaction-held lock ordering in sibling financial workflows, supporting that the shared helper contract is deliberate.
The purchase lock statement occurs before the explicit transaction in source; exact SQL Server autocommit lock lifetime and an actual competing-spend outcome were not run in this audit.
This comparison covers these named call sites only; the other TreasuryBalanceQuery callers are not all reviewed here.
recommendation: No new canonical finding is created; extend/retain FIN-011. Future correction should move the protected-balance read and assertion into ReceivePurchaseHandler’s already existing transaction, immediately before writing the treasury movement, while retaining the shared idempotency/journal and atomic purchase/stock/supplier writes. Also confirm the business-day cutoff policy separately; this comparison concerns account balance locking.

needed: Provider-backed concurrency test: seed a protected account balance, pause ReceivePurchase after current precheck, commit a competing withdrawal/payment, then resume; assert overspend cannot pass after the transaction-held lock is applied.
Interleave two positive PaidPiastres purchase receipts with different request IDs against one source account and assert aggregate posted outflow never exceeds available protected balance.
Retain same-request replay test and assert purchase, payment, supplier-ledger, stock-receipt and journal rows are each written once.
Regression test zero-paid and non-cash purchase paths to preserve legitimate account and balance semantics.

quality.source_read: All listed ranges read in source for the two principal workflows, the shared lock helper and two inside-transaction control callers.
quality.baseline: Current Source-Symbol index identity and worktree hashes checked for each source file.
quality.independent_review: No other agent independently challenged this specific comparison in this batch; it cross-references existing FIN-011 evidence.
